frontier.hypothesis: Loop 2's clause-B consumer can be a use of the preheader addend inside loop 2's BODY, which is a later extended basic block (the loop top is a branch target, so cse starts a fresh EBB there) - and therefore forces materialisation of the copy - provided the body use is one whose instruction target already emits. Build on cell W1 (the self-clobbering `t2` guard, 3 at 127/127), which supplies the add-survival half of the predicate for free; every prior body-use measurement (s19's Z1-Z5, s15's C1/D1) was taken on the INLINE-guard chassis where the base add is merged away, so none of them tested this combination.
frontier.mechanism: E-s20-1: cse can only rewrite uses inside the EBB it is processing. Loop 2's body begins at a branch target (`.jump` label 171), so any use of the preheader addend there is un-rewritable and cse must leave `DST = SRC` in the preheader. E-s20-2 (satisfied by W1) keeps the base add alive so the copy lands in front of it rather than being merged away. The open question is purely which body use survives cse's re-canonicalisation back to `base + i` without adding an instruction.
frontier.next_probe: On the W1 chassis, name loop 2's preheader addend (`q2 = *(u8 **)(ctx + 0xC); base = (u8 *)(sh2 + (s32)q2);`) and sweep body spellings that consume q2 rather than base: (a) the element read as `*(u8 *)(q2 + sh2 + i + 0x2C)`, (b) the back-edge limit as `*(s32 *)((s32)q2 + sh2 + 0x20)`, (c) the element read associated as `(q2 + i) + sh2`, (d) each of (a)-(c) with the loop rotated so the limit read is the last body statement. Score every cell with `sandbox --disable all`, and for any cell at 127 read `.cse` (via pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1) to check whether insn 162's analogue survived as a copy - a surviving copy with the base add intact is the win even if the cell's own score is not yet 3.

frontier.hypothesis: Target satisfies the materialisation predicate with NO later-EBB use of the copy destination anywhere in its listing (a3 appears exactly 5 times: the prologue home of arg3 and the copy/base pair in each loop). Since E-s20-1 says cse cannot leave a copy without such a use, target's copy must come from cse DECLINING to substitute at the base add - i.e. reg79 was not the canonical member of its quantity at that point (E-s16-2). Naming the exact canon_reg/qty_first_reg condition would turn every remaining spelling into a checkable predicate rather than a guess.
frontier.mechanism: cse.c canonicalises a register operand to qty_first_reg[reg_qty[regno]] (canon_reg). qty_first_reg can MOVE when a class member is invalidated (delete_reg_equiv / invalidate), and insert / merge_equiv_classes decides membership order. If the guard's read and the preheader's read end up in the same quantity but with the PREHEADER's pseudo first, cse substitutes reg80 at the base add and leaves the guard's reg79 - producing a copy with no later-EBB use, which is exactly target's shape.
frontier.next_probe: Add a BB2_CSE_DEBUG trace in canon_reg / insert / merge_equiv_classes / invalidate printing (insn uid, regno, reg_qty, qty_first_reg) for pseudos in the 72-170 range; rebuild ONLY tools/gcc-2.7.2/cc1 (never build/cc1); re-prove codegen identity on the whole TU with tmp/grind/func_80017848/s16/idump.sh; then diff the traces of the V1 candidate, cell U1 and cell W1 at loop 1's insn 83/89 and loop 2's insn 162/168. s17 deprioritised this on the grounds that a confirmed predicate had no affordable C carrier - that grounds is now weaker, because W1 supplies the add-survival half for free and the body-use family in frontier item 1 is an untested carrier.

frontier.hypothesis: The 3-instruction residual may be reachable by paying the materialisation cost for loop 2 in a slot target fills with a MOVE rather than a load. Target's listing contains no move in loop 2's exit region, but it does contain `addu v0,a0,v1` immediately at loop 2's exit (T.txt, the strength-reduced element pointer) - if loop 2's clause-B consumer can be folded into that induction-variable update rather than added beside it, the purchase is genuinely free.
frontier.mechanism: E-s20-1 requires only that SOME later-EBB insn read the copy's destination. GCC's strength reduction already materialises `base + i` at loop 2's exit (`addu v0,a0,v1`); if the C is spelled so that this exit value is expressed in terms of the preheader addend rather than base, the existing insn becomes the un-rewritable use and no new instruction is needed. s18's cell W2 measured an EXPLICIT walking element pointer at 14, but that wrote the pointer as a loop-carried local; the untested form is a single post-loop expression that reads the addend.
frontier.next_probe: On the W1 chassis, after loop 2's do/while add a post-loop expression that reads q2 and whose value target already computes at that point - e.g. carry the element pointer out as `end = (u8 *)((s32)q2 + sh2 + i);` and then use `end` for nothing but the immediately following math-arg base derivation - and sweep whether GCC folds it onto the existing `addu v0,a0,v1` or emits a new insn. Score with sandbox and confirm the insn count stays 127 before reading any dump.
